conviction_note: The weightiest fact is the BCRA's own Q3 2026 system data, published 20 Nov, a week after the last consensus snapshot. System ROA fell from 2.5% annualised in Q2 to 0.8% in Q3, and private domestic banks fell from about 1.75% to about 0.5%, driven by a lower financial margin. Supervielle's Q3 confirms the pattern: net income -50% QoQ, NIM -430bp. Against that, the Bloomberg consensus of ARS219.5bn implies flat real profit. Three things offset it: asset quality is visibly turning (lower NPL, lower loan-loss charges), the bar is disputed (Citi has ARS188.5bn, Goldman -19% real recurring profit), and the ADR is already -7.4% in 5 days at a 52-week low with a buyback running. So p_up is 43, not lower. The findings sum to -0.8 and the scaled number is -0.63; the two agree in sign and size. Guidance moves only on the 30 Nov call, after the window, which limits the reaction in the window.
bar: Disputed. Bloomberg consensus Q3 2026 net income ARS219.521bn against Citi ARS188.511bn, both per iProfesional 2026-11-13 (https://www.iprofesional.com/finanzas/468851-wall-street-recomienda-una-sola-accion-entre-los-bancos-argentinos). Goldman (same article): Q3 ROE 11.2%, recurring profit -19% real QoQ, NIM 17.6% to 16.3%, NII -6%, delinquency 6.1%. Q2 2026 reported ARS206.8bn, about ARS219bn restated for Q3 inflation (~5.8%); ARS221bn adjusted for ARS21.9bn restructuring (https://pulse2.com/banco-macro-npl-ratio-more-than-triples-yoy-to-6-25-even-as-net-income-rises-39-sequentially/). So the Bloomberg consensus is roughly flat real QoQ while the two named brokers sit 14-18% below it. Company guide: 2026 adjusted ROE about 12%, reported 9-10%; NPL 5.5-6% by year end from 6.25%; cost of risk 6.5-7% (https://quartr.com/events/banco-macro-s-a-bma-q2-2026_F36oi3NT). Because two sources disagree, findings that depend on the bar are capped small. print_vs_bar_pct is measured against the ARS219.5bn Bloomberg figure.
positioning_check: Short interest is low and not crowded: about 672k shares short, 2.4 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-30 (https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/BMA/short-interest); 3.1% of float and rising per Benzinga, updated 2026-10-26 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BMA/sentiment). No squeeze mechanism. Baseline: skew_25d null and the option chain unusable (ATM spread 112% of mid, total OI 112, put/call OI 0.62, ATM IV 65.1% for 18 Dec). Tape: -7.36% in 5d, -17.06% in 20d, -52.3% from the 52-week high, 0.16% above the 52-week low. YTD to 2026-10-29: -33.3% in USD (https://eleconomista.com.ar/finanzas/para-olvido-acciones-argentinas-desploman-42-dolares-ano-n99317/amp). Company buyback active (6 tranches, ~3.0m Class B shares bought through 2026-11-24). The run-up already leans negative, so a negative finding agrees with the price and is partly priced.

findings.finding: The BCRA's Informe sobre Bancos for September 2026, published 2026-11-20, puts the whole system's Q3 2026 ROA at 0.8% annualised (ROE 3.4%), against 2.5% in Q2 (June report, published 2026-08-21). Chart 17 shows private domestic banks (EFB priv. nac., the group that holds Macro, Galicia and Supervielle) at about 0.5% 3m ROA to September, against about 1.75% for Q2 in the June report's Chart 15. The BCRA attributes the decline mainly to a lower 'margen financiero integral', partly offset by lower loan-loss charges, admin expenses and taxes. The Bloomberg consensus of ARS219.5bn implies Macro's real profit flat QoQ.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 (released 2026-02-25 amc): headline net income ARS100.1bn against a ARS164.3bn Bloomberg consensus (-39%, one-offs ARS82.9bn). The ADR fell 7.3% the next day with GGAL -4.8% and SUPV -6.8%, so about -2.5 points of excess (https://www.bloomberglinea.com/latinoamerica/argentina/banco-macro-vuelve-al-verde-pero-no-alcanza-estimaciones-de-wall-street-en-el-cuarto-trimestre/ ; https://www.riotimesonline.com/argentinas-merval-sinks-1-6-to-3-month-low-as-banks-crash-up-to-7). Q2 2026 beat (released 2026-08-19 amc, +5% vs BofA, +22% vs JPM): local share -2.2% on 08-20 and +1.8% on 08-21 (https://www.rava.com/cotizaciones/historico/bma/2026/08).
findings.why_not_priced: The only dated consensus (ARS219.5bn, as of 2026-11-13) predates this release, and implies Macro held its real Q2 profit while the system lost about two-thirds of its ROA. The numbers sit in a Spanish PDF chart and drew no wire coverage I could find. If the market had fully priced it, the consensus would sit near or below Citi's ARS188.5bn and previews would flag a sharp QoQ drop. Partial pricing is visible: the ADR is -7.4% over the five sessions since publication and at a 52-week low, though country risk and the sector moved too. Sized small because it is a system aggregate (a proxy for Macro), Macro earned about twice the private-domestic group ROA in Q2 (3.3% vs ~1.75%), and the bar is disputed.
findings.independence: Supervielle's Q3 print (separate finding, separate document) shows the same margin compression: NIM -430bp, NFI -22.4% QoQ (https://grafa.com/en/news/united-states/grupo-supervielle-q3-2026-results-net-income-falls). Goldman's Macro preview also expects NIM 17.6% to 16.3% and recurring profit -19% real (iProfesional 2026-11-13). Supervielle is inside the BCRA aggregate, so the two overlap; they are sized separately and smaller for that reason.

findings.finding: Grupo Supervielle, the first of the four Argentine bank ADRs to report Q3 2026 (story dated 2026-11-17), printed net income of ARS6.8bn, about half of Q2's ARS13.6bn, ROAE 2.2%. Net financial income fell 22.4% QoQ and NIM fell 430bp to 16%. EPS was $0.08 against a $0.16 consensus, and 2026 ROE guidance was cut for the fourth straight quarter, to 1-2% reported and 5-6% adjusted. Offsets in the same print: NPL improved to 5.4%, loan-loss provisions fell 14.5% QoQ, and opex fell 26.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No dated record of BMA's reaction to a peer's print. On Macro's own prints the margin line drove the Q4 2025 miss (-7.3% ADR with the sector) and the Q2 2026 beat (muted).
findings.why_not_priced: Public for about a week, so largely priced in the sector; BMA has fallen since. Supervielle is a weaker, more retail-funded bank (Q2 ROE 4.4% vs Macro 13.4%), so its margin hit transmits only partly. If it had moved Macro's bar, Bloomberg's ARS219.5bn would have been revised; I found no later figure.
findings.independence: Overlaps the BCRA aggregate (finding 1), which includes Supervielle. Margin-guidance detail from the earnings-whispers transcript (https://www.earningswhispers.com/transcript/SUPV/Q32026).

findings.finding: Asset quality is turning in the system data Macro's Q3 will mirror. BCRA September 2026: private-sector NPL fell 0.25pp to 7.50%; household NPL fell 0.61pp to 12.20%, its second monthly decline; the irregular balance fell 2.58% real, the first negative since April 2024; estimated PD fell a fourth month to 2.04%; provision coverage rose to 88.2%. Macro guided NPL to 5.5-6% by year end from 6.25% in Q2, and its book is consumer-heavy (consumer NPL 8.42% in Q2), where the improvement is concentrated. The system figure is helped by write-offs and refinancing (households refinanced 3.9% of the book; 24.1% of irregular balances refinanced).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NPL was the line analysts flagged after Q2 2026 (SBS: 'monitoring delinquency will be essential'; NPL 6.25% from 5.4%) when the local share went -2.2% then +1.8% (https://www.iprofesional.com/finanzas/462851-que-hacer-con-las-acciones-de-banco-macro-tras-su-balance). In Q2 2026 Galicia printed lower loan-loss charges and its ADR still fell (https://www.bloomberglinea.com/latinoamerica/argentina/galicia-sale-del-rojo-y-destaca-menor-cargo-por-incobrabilidad-pero-acciones-ceden-en-wall-street/).
findings.why_not_priced: Goldman's preview still carries Macro delinquency at 6.1%, roughly flat, and the 52-week-low price shows no credit-turn optimism. A first QoQ NPL decline with lower cost of risk would be the quality-of-earnings offset to a margin miss. If it were priced, the sector would have bounced on the Nov 20 report; it fell instead. Partly an inference from system to company, and some of the improvement is write-offs, so sized modestly.
findings.independence: Supervielle's Q3: NPL improved to 5.4% and provisions fell 14.5% QoQ (https://grafa.com/en/news/united-states/grupo-supervielle-q3-2026-results-net-income-falls). Forbes Argentina 2026-10-29 on household NPL declining from August (https://www.forbesargentina.com/money/la-mora-bancaria-empieza-bajar-banco-central-ya-habla-fin-ciclo-atrasos-n101351). Shares the BCRA document with finding 1, but reads a different line (credit cost vs margin).

findings.finding: Macro is buying back its own stock into the print. The program was announced 2026-10-29: up to ARS160bn and 20m Class B shares, max price ARS10,700, 45 days. Six disclosed tranches had bought about 3.0m shares for about ARS28.6bn (about 15% of the share cap) by 2026-11-24; the latest was 430,000 shares at about ARS9,251. The local share closed at ARS9,100 on 11-24, well under the ARS10,700 cap. The company said the price does not reflect fundamentals.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior buyback-into-print episode found for BMA.
findings.why_not_priced: The program is public (6-Ks), so the level is priced. What is not priced is the support it gives the local Thursday session (BYMA trades on US Thanksgiving) and hence the ADR's Friday half-day. It is capped at 25% of 90-day average volume, so the support is small.
findings.independence: Program terms per El Economista 2026-10-29 (https://eleconomista.com.ar/finanzas/uno-bancos-mas-grandes-pais-anuncia-una-millonaria-recompra-acciones-n99320); daily tranche filings listed on Rava (https://www.rava.com/noticias?ticker=BMA_US). Panabee's cumulative totals are its own arithmetic over the 6-Ks.

findings.finding: More restructuring charges are likely in the headline. Q2 2026 carried ARS21.9bn pre-tax (ARS14.2bn after tax) of early-retirement and severance costs. Management's reported 2026 ROE guide of 9-10% sits below the 12% adjusted guide, implying more charges in H2. Q4 2025 shows such charges can turn the headline into a large 'miss' (-39% vs consensus on ARS82.9bn of one-offs).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025: one-offs drove a -39% headline miss; the ADR was +0.1% after hours, then -7.3% the next day in a sector-wide selloff (GGAL -4.8%).
findings.why_not_priced: The guide gap is public, but it is unclear whether the Bloomberg consensus is on a reported or adjusted basis. A headline-vs-consensus gap from charges sets the first after-hours read. Below the line with no path to the guide, so sized at a fraction.

outside_window.finding: A cut to the 2026 adjusted-ROE guide (about 12%, raised from 8% in Q2) is likely given the system's Q3 ROA collapse, mirroring Supervielle's fourth straight cut. Macro gives guidance on the call, not in the press release, and the call is 2026-11-30 11:00 NY, after the reaction session closes on 2026-11-27.

baseline_tension: No usable skew; the tape leans negative (-17% in 20 days, at a 52-week low) and my negative findings agree with it. That makes them partly priced, which is why p_up is 43 and not lower. The asset-quality turn and the buyback are the evidence against the run-up.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed: Bloomberg ARS219.5bn vs Citi ARS188.5bn): the BCRA system-ROA finding, which reads through to a miss vs consensus, was cut from -2.0 to -1.5.

Rule 5 (macro/system-to-company transmission is a proxy): the same finding stays filed at the smaller size and its independence names it as a proxy; it is not doubled with the Supervielle read, which was trimmed from -0.5 to -0.4 for overlap.
Rule 2 (one-offs below the line): the restructuring-charge finding was cut from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 6 (exit window): guidance moves only on the 2026-11-30 call, so the guide-cut risk stays in outside_window (unchanged from the draft).
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest about 3% of float and 2.4 days to cover, so no squeeze adjustment; the agreement with a negative run-up moves p_up from 42 to 43.
Rule 1 (reaction function): Macro's Q2 beat was met with a muted/negative local reaction and its Q4 2025 miss fell with the sector, so the sizes stay small; the asset-quality positive is unchanged.
